title: CAST: Modeling Visual State Transitions for Consistent Video Retrieval
claim: Context-agnostic retrieval returns semantically plausible but state- or identity-inconsistent results; modeling the latent state transition yields temporally coherent continuations.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: context, latent-shift arrow with vector diagram, result grid with check/cross marks
description: The figure has three columns that read left to right. The left gray panel, 'Input Context & Query', shows a stack of three kitchen video frames (V_{t-3}, V_{t-2}, V_{t-1}) braced as 'Visual History (H_t)'. Below it is an orange box reading 'Query: slice the tomatoes'. The middle panel, 'Latent Shift', is a large gray arrow containing a small vector diagram. A blue vector goes from V_{t-1}, an orange vector labeled Δ(q,v) follows it, and a green dashed line ends at v̂_t. caption: Given a context clip and instruction, standard retrieval often returns semantically relevant but temporally incoherent clips, yielding State Errors or Identity Errors. In contrast, CAST models the state transition (Δ) to retrieve a causally plausible continuation and rerank generation candidates toward more coherent continuations.
abstract: As video content creation shifts toward long-form narratives, composing short clips into coherent storylines becomes increasingly important. However, prevailing retrieval formulations remain context-agnostic at inference time, prioritizing local semantic alignment while neglecting state and identity consistency. To address this structural limitation, we formalize the task of Consistent Video Retrieval (CVR) and introduce a diagnostic benchmark spanning YouCook2, COIN, and CrossTask. We propose CAST (Context-Aware State Transition), a lightweight, plug-and-play adapter compatible with diverse frozen vision-language embedding spaces. By predicting a state-conditioned residual update ($Î$) from visual history, CAST introduces an explicit inductive bias for latent state evolution. Extensive experiments show that CAST improves performance on YouCook2 and CrossTask, remains competitive on COIN, and consistently outperforms zero-shot baselines across diverse foundation backbones. Furthermore, CAST provides a useful reranking signal for black-box video generation candidates (e.g., from Veo), promoting more temporally coherent continuations.
